complexity_scope.guarantee: For every fixed oblivious bounded convex L-Lipschitz sequence; expectation over independent sphere directions.
complexity_scope.hidden_constants: Displayed coefficient 2 and all R,d,C,L,r dependence are explicit; no suppressed reshaping or projection costs.
complexity_scope.oracle: One exact cost value c_t(x_t) at the played point per round; separate exact Euclidean projection onto the shrunk set.
complexity_scope.output_and_metric: Online played sequence x_1,...,x_n∈S; expected static regret against the best single hindsight point in S. No last-iterate optimization guarantee.
complexity_scope.regime: Original coordinates with supplied r,R; d,n≥1; C>0, L≥0; delta<r with the stated tuning.
complexity_scope.resource: n cost observations, n independent sphere samples and n projections if Figure 1 is executed literally, including its final unused state update. Projection runtime and geometric preprocessing are not included in the cost-value count.
complexity_scope.upper_witness_or_lower_coverage: Only Figure 1 BGD with the displayed Theorem 2 tuning; no unrestricted Oracle Complexity lower bound or optimality claim.

map: Observation 2 gives feasibility when delta≤alpha r and alpha<1, since (1−alpha)S+alpha rB_d⊆S.

Apply Lemma 1 to ball-smoothed costs with sphere estimator g_t=(d/delta)c_t(y_t+delta u_t)u_t. Conditional on the center, its mean is the smoothed gradient and ||g_t||≤dC/delta. In the source's Theorem 1 proof, x/y notation changes; this map consistently uses Figure 1's y_t as center and x_t as play.
Lemma 2 uses convexity, projection nonexpansiveness and the squared-distance potential; eta=nu delta/d=R/[(dC/delta)sqrt(n)] yields smoothed regret at most RdC sqrt(n)/delta.
The Lipschitz bound controls smoothing and play displacement; Observation 1 controls shrinking the comparator set. Eq. (10) gives R_n≤RdC sqrt(n)/delta+3delta L n+2alpha Cn.
Theorem 2 substitutes its displayed delta, alpha and nu into this bound, obtaining the stated upper bound. Its printed proof explicitly refers back to the Theorem 1 proof and Eq. (10).
proofs.omitted_details: This is a faithful source proof map, not an independently reconstructed full proof. Boundary regularity and source notation are recorded as use cautions; no certification of every printed intermediate formula is claimed.

assumptions: rB_d⊆S⊆RB_d with 0<r≤R; closedness is an explicit well-posedness restriction for the selected extraction.
Every c_t:S→[-C,C] is convex and L-Lipschitz in the Euclidean norm.
The loss sequence is fixed in advance, independent of the algorithm's private directions; only the played-point value is observed.
Exact projection onto (1−alpha)S is available as a separate operation.
Use nu=R/(C sqrt(n)), delta=n^(−1/4)sqrt(R d C r/[3(Lr+C)]), alpha=delta/r, and restrict to delta<r. The source states n sufficiently large; the explicit inequality is the selected feasible regime.
statement.conclusion: Every played point x_t lies in S and R_n≤2 n^(3/4)sqrt(3 R d C (L+C/r)).
statement.objects_and_definitions: Let S⊂R^d be a closed convex feasible set, B_d the Euclidean unit ball and P_K exact nearest-point projection onto K. For a fixed sequence c_1,...,c_n define R_n=E[sum_{t=1}^n c_t(x_t)]−min_{z∈S}sum_{t=1}^n c_t(z). Use y_1=0, fresh independent uniform unit vectors u_t, x_t=y_t+delta u_t, observe c_t(x_t), and y_{t+1}=P_{(1−alpha)S}(y_t−nu c_t(x_t)u_t).
statement.parameter_domains: d,n positive integers; C>0, 0<r≤R, L≥0; delta and alpha as specified with 0<delta<r and 0<alpha<1.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every such S, parameters and fixed loss sequence, the prescribed randomized BGD has the stated regret. Expectation is over its independently sampled sphere directions only. This is not a guarantee for an adaptive adversary.
